description: An open-source bastion host (jump server) for SSH, RDP, VNC and Telnet with web access, session recording, audit logs and Casdoor SSO

latest_release.name: v2.0.0
latest_release.body:
## Changelog
### Features
* 9cee10808eaac677b30807981b092224564406d4 feat: add system accounts with password rotation, and access requests that administrators approve
* 380805e5bb91d23ab0057c1a7368c22ddc10dcc0 feat: connect to MySQL and PostgreSQL assets in the browser and audit the SQL
* 8fc8a993fa042ca90555109fa8fdf7bd37a27d7b feat: copy images and files between the browser and RDP sessions through the clipboard
* 9b9395f6f1bba51a930706dbbd5cf21233dc2b33 feat: export audit logs as CSV and forward them to syslog
* 0846eaa801d77ba1bddb3555e6d6e2eab769593a feat: forward local ports to RDP, VNC and other assets through the SSH gateway
* 5acab8848a4e4d5422eded74d9d9f59ab2565dd0 feat: put an image copied on this machine on the RDP clipboard when the page gets the focus
* e32ce38a5e75c3dfb09a715e05a734c1edad6e14 feat: run commands, scripts and file transfers on many SSH assets at once
* 033f120b6994726feb5f76324a9a6a09438b0147 feat: serve the Go profiles on a local address when pprofAddr is set
* 500a3f839d187a60ec8e3b9abaa3c88dd6481ba1 feat: sign in to local accounts with a code from an authenticator app
### Bug fixes
* c8c795aaedff2310f212ffe086bf486488240a9d fix: close the RDP viewer when the session ends and reconnect after a dropped connection
* 56c19a475eeb3e70076e09fa9ceb77321e45c176 fix: hold the VNC clipboard and gateway commands to the clipboard and file permissions
* 593fbffae0231de9d43a8795866187331dfa7431 fix: keep Chrome from freezing background connection pages, which closes their WebSockets
* 6ed7c4c9f2db77cf5a66320a30b7ebd17df483c5 fix: keep retrying with a growing delay when reconnecting to an RDP session fails
* 6dc603047979daa88905e5c22afd22de8c8b1b76 fix: let approvals only narrow access requests and check database exports against the session's account
* a4cc1b332d116f8f10591f6f2e7d6220851dd465 fix: release keys the RDP screen lost the release of, so Ctrl does not stay down
* 3a4f889cce680eb311f2bd17230c7c8d52ee8964 fix: reload connection pages left open across a server upgrade

detail.readme:
An open-source bastion host (jump server) for SSH, RDP, VNC, Telnet and databases

Casvisor gives your team one place to reach servers, desktops and databases from the browser.
It connects over SSH, RDP, VNC, Telnet, MySQL and PostgreSQL, with an SSH gateway for ssh, scp and VS Code,
and records every session, checks every command and keeps the passwords to itself.

Website · Documentation · Live demo · Discord

SSH and VNC in the browser, with rm -rf / stopped by a command rule and every command on record.

Session replay. Play back SSH, Telnet, VNC and RDP sessions in the browser, with the commands beside them. Command records. Every command and SQL statement, and which rule blocked or flagged it. Permissions. Who can reach which assets, from where, until when and with which actions.
## 🚀 Try it in 30 seconds No database and no config file needed. This runs Casvisor on SQLite with its own accounts: ```bash docker run -d --name casvisor -p 19000:19000 -p 2222:2222 \ -v casvisor-db:/db -v casvisor-recordings:/recordings casbin/casvisor docker logs casvisor ``` Open and sign in: | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Username | `admin` | | Password | the one printed in `docker logs casvisor` | > Pass `-e adminPassword=` to choose the first password instead. Either way, change it under **My Account** after you sign in. Prefer not to install anything? The hosted demo at **[demo.casvisor.com](https://demo.casvisor.com)** comes with a sandboxed Linux shell (SSH) and a private desktop (VNC) to connect to. Nothing there touches a real server, sessions end after 15 minutes, and each visitor can keep two sessions open at a time. ## 🤔 Why Casvisor Casvisor sits between the people who run your servers and the servers themselves. People open sessions from a browser tab, or with their own `ssh`, `scp` and VS Code through the SSH gateway. They only reach the servers and databases a permission gives them, and never see the stored passwords. - **One Go binary.** Casvisor speaks SSH, RDP, VNC, Telnet, MySQL and PostgreSQL itself, with nothing to install on the servers. It runs on SQLite with its own accounts out of the box. - **Apache-2.0, no enterprise edition.** Recording, the SSH gateway, network gateways, system accounts, jobs and everything else in this README are in the open-source project. - **Policy you can read.** Permissions are enforced with [Casbin](https://casbin.apache.org), and sign-in can be handed to [Casdoor](https://casdoor.ai) for SSO, MFA, LDAP and social logins. - **Audit by default.** Sessions are recorded, commands and SQL statements are checked against your rules and logged, and the logs export to CSV or a syslog server. Coming from another bastion host? See how Casvisor [compares with JumpServer, Teleport and others](https://casvisor.org/docs/more/comparison). ## 📦 Installation Three supported paths, fastest first. All of them end up at . ### Docker ```bash docker run -d --name casvisor -p 19000:19000 -p 2222:2222 \ -v casvisor-db:/db -v casvisor-recordings:/recordings casbin/casvisor ``` Port 19000 is the web console and port 2222 is the SSH gateway. The two volumes keep the database and the session recordings when the container is replaced. Guide: [Quick start](https://casvisor.org/docs/getting-started/quickstart) ### Docker Compose [`docker-compose.yml`](docker-compose.yml) builds the image from this repository and runs it with the same ports and volumes: ```bash docker compose up -d ``` Set `adminPassword` in the compose file to choose the first password of `admin`; when it is empty, a random one is printed in the log. ### From source — for development Use this if you intend to modify Casvisor. Prerequisites: **Go 1.23+** (see [`go.mod`](go.mod)), **Node.js 20 LTS** and **Yarn 1.x**. ```bash git clone https://github.com/casvisor/casvisor cd casvisor/web && yarn install && yarn build && cd .. go run main.go ``` Guide: [Build from source](https://casvisor.org/docs/getting-started/source) ### Configuration Settings are read from [`conf/app.conf`](conf/app.conf). Put the settings of your own server in `conf/app.local.conf` (same format, not tracked by git), or pass any of them as environment variables. **Database.** The default is SQLite. To use MySQL instead (the database is created if it does not exist): ```ini driverName = mysql dataSourceName = root:123456@tcp(localhost:3306)/ dbName = casvisor ``` **Sign in with Casdoor.** Instead of its own accounts, Casvisor can sign users in with [Casdoor](https://casdoor.ai), for SSO, MFA, LDAP and third-party logins, and use Casdoor's groups in permissions. Create an organization and an application for Casvisor in Casdoor, add `http:///callback` to the redirect URLs of the application, and set: ```ini casdoorEndpoint = https:// clientId = clientSecret = casdoorOrganization = casdoorApplication = ``` When `casdoorEndpoint` is empty, Casvisor uses its own accounts. **Recordings.** Sessions are recorded to `recordings/` under the working directory (`/recordings` in Docker). `recordingPath` moves them, `recordingRetentionDays` deletes the ones older than that many days, and `disableRecording = true` turns recording off. Guide: [Configuration](https://casvisor.org/docs/operations/configuration) · [Sign in with Casdoor](https://casvisor.org/docs/getting-started/casdoor) · [Behind a reverse proxy](https://casvisor.org/docs/operations/reverse-proxy) ## 👉 After you sign in At this point you have a running bastion host with nothing behind it yet. Next: 1. **Change the `admin` password** under **My Account**, and turn on two-step verification there. 2. **[Add an asset](https://casvisor.org/docs/assets/assets)** under **Assets** (a server, a desktop or a database) and click **Connect**. Administrators reach every asset. 3. **[Let other people in](https://casvisor.org/docs/access-control/permissions)**: add them under **Users** and give them a **Permission** on assets or asset tags. 4. **[Use the SSH gateway](https://casvisor.org/docs/assets/ssh-gateway)**: users add their public key under **SSH keys** and connect with `ssh -p 2222 @`. 5. **[Add command rules](https://casvisor.org/docs/audit/commands)** to block or flag commands such as `rm -rf /` or `DROP DATABASE`. ## ✨ Features **🔌 Connect** - **SSH** — an xterm.js terminal in the browser, with a file panel beside it for upload and download over SFTP - **RDP** — [gordp](https://github.com/casvisor/gordp), a pure-Go RDP client: NLA, the GFX graphics pipeline (ClearCodec, RemoteFX Progressive) like the Windows client, sharp text on high-DPI screens, the remote cursor, clipboard with text, images and files, resizing with the window, and file transfer through a redirected drive. Works with Windows Server, Windows 10/11 and FreeRDP-based hosts such as Ubuntu - **VNC** — noVNC in the browser; Casvisor does the VNC authentication itself, so the password stays on the server - **Telnet** — for network gear and old systems, logging in with the asset's account - **MySQL and PostgreSQL** — a browser SQL console with the databases, tables and columns on the left, one tab per result, and CSV export - **SSH gateway** — `ssh -p 2222 web-01@casvisor.example.com`, `scp`, `sftp`, `rsync`, Xshell and VS Code Remote, signed in with the user's public key and under the same permissions as the browser - **Port forwarding to any asset** — `ssh -p 2222 -N -L 13389:win-01:3389 alice@casvisor.example.com`, then mstsc, a VNC viewer or a database client connects to `localhost:13389` - **Network gateways** — reach assets in another data center or behind NAT, through an SSH jump host or an agent that connects out over HTTPS - **Stored credentials** — passwords and private keys are encrypted in the database and filled in by Casvisor; SSH host keys and RDP certificates are pinned on first use **🛡️ Control** - **Permissions** — on users, groups, assets and asset tags, with the actions `Connect`, `Copy`, `Paste`, `Upload`, `Download` and `Forward`, client IP ranges and a time window - **System accounts** — several accounts per asset, such as `root`, `deploy` and `readonly`; permissions decide which one a user may connect with, and passwords can be changed by hand or on a schedule - **Access requests** — users ask for an asset with a reason and an end time, an administrator approves, and withdrawing it disconnects open sessions - **Two-step verification** — for local accounts, with any TOTP authenticator app - **Command rules** — block or flag commands matching a regular expression, in the web terminal, the SQL console and through the SSH gateway alike - **Revocation takes effect at once** — open sessions are disconnected as soon as their permission or account is edited, deleted or expires **🔍 Audit** - **Session recording and playback** — SSH, Telnet, VNC and RDP, replayed in the browser with the same code that drew them live; SSH and Telnet recordings download as asciicast - **Live monitoring** — watch online sessions and stop any of them - **Command records** — SSH and Telnet commands are read off a virtual screen, so tab completion, history and line edits are captured as they ran; SQL statements are logged too - **Operation log** — file transfers and every change made through the API - **Export and syslog** — session, command and operation logs export to CSV and can be forwarded to a syslog server as RFC 5424 JSON or CEF **⚙️ Operate** - **Jobs** — run a command, a Bash or PowerShell script, or a file copy on many SSH assets at once, with concurrency, timeouts and per-asset output and exit codes - **Patch management** — scan SSH assets for pending system updates, install them and restart, on Windows (Windows Update) and Linux (apt, dnf, yum) - **REST API** — every console action is also an API call, with [Swagger docs](swagger) - **Web console** — in 9 languages, built with React, Vite and shadcn/ui ## 🌐 Network gateways Assets in another data center, or behind NAT in an office, are reached through a network gateway. Add one under **Network gateways** and pick it in the asset's **Network gateway** field. Every connection to the asset (web SSH, Telnet, VNC, RDP, databases, the SSH gateway and patch management) then goes through it. - **SSH jump host**: a server in that network that Casvisor can log in to over SSH. Nothing is installed on it; its sshd needs `AllowTcpForwarding yes`. - **Agent**: for networks Casvisor cannot connect into at all. Generate a token on the gateway's page and run the agent on any machine in that network: ```bash casvisor agent --server https://casvisor.example.com --token cva_... --fingerprint SHA256:... ``` The agent is the same `casvisor` binary (with Docker: `docker run -d --restart unless-stopped casbin/casvisor agent --server ...`). It connects out to Casvisor's web address over WebSocket, so it works wherever HTTPS gets out, listens on no port, and only connects to the **Allowed networks** set on the gateway. Guide: [Network gateways](https://casvisor.org/docs/assets/network-gateways) ## 🧱 Technology stack Casvisor is a frontend–backend separated application: - **Backend** — Go with the [Beego](https://github.com/beego/beego) framework: the REST API, the protocol tunnels and the SSH gateway ([repository root](https://github.com/casvisor/casvisor)) - **Frontend** — React with [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/) on Tailwind CSS, built with Vite: the console, the workbench and the session player ([`web/`](web)) - **RDP** — [casvisor/gordp](https://github.com/casvisor/gordp), a pure-Go RDP client - **Authorization** — [Casbin](https://casbin.apache.org) - **Database** — SQLite or MySQL through [XORM](https://xorm.io/) ## 📖 Documentation The full documentation lives at **[casvisor.org](https://casvisor.org/docs)**. Common starting points: | I want to… | Go to | |------------|-------| | Install Casvisor | [Quick start](https://casvisor.org/docs/getting-started/quickstart) · [From source](https://casvisor.org/docs/getting-started/source) | | Connect to servers and databases | [Protocols](https://casvisor.org/docs/assets/protocols) · [Databases](https://casvisor.org/docs/assets/databases) · [SSH gateway](https://casvisor.org/docs/assets/ssh-gateway) | | Decide who can reach what | [Permissions](https://casvisor.org/docs/access-control/permissions) · [Access requests](https://casvisor.org/docs/access-control/access-requests) | | Review what people did | [Recordings](https://casvisor.org/docs/audit/recordings) · [Commands](https://casvisor.org/docs/audit/commands) · [Export](https://casvisor.org/docs/audit/export) | | Run it in production | [Configuration](https://casvisor.org/docs/operations/configuration) · [Reverse proxy](https://casvisor.org/docs/operations/reverse-proxy) · [Upgrading](https://casvisor.org/docs/operations/upgrading) | ## 🔒 Security **Please do not report security vulnerabilities in public GitHub issues.** Email instead. Before exposing a Casvisor instance to the internet: - Change the `admin` password and turn on two-step verification, or sign in through Casdoor. - Serve Casvisor over HTTPS only, behind a reverse proxy, and set `trustedProxies` and `allowedOrigins` in [`conf/app.conf`](conf/app.conf). - Keep port 2222 (the SSH gateway) closed to networks that do not need it. - Back up the credential key with the database: stored passwords and private keys cannot be decrypted without it. It is `credentialKey` in the config, or `credential.key` next to the SQLite database when that is not set. ## 🤝 Community and support - **Discord** — [join the community](https://discord.gg/yfKcuHVAHB) for questions and help - **GitHub Issues** — [bug reports and feature requests](https://github.com/casvisor/casvisor/issues) ## 🌍 Contributing Contributions are welcome. For anything larger than a small fix, **please open an issue first** so you can agree on the approach with the maintainers before writing code. **Translations.** User-facing strings in the web console go through [i18next](https://www.i18next.com/). After adding or changing one under [`web/`](web), run `go test -tags manual ./i18n -run TestGenerateI18nStrings` to add the new keys to every catalog in [`web/src/locales/`](web/src/locales), then translate them. ## 📄 License Casvisor is licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE). ---
